nodes.label: Two-Tier Architecture (core 0 command source / core 1 flight loop)
nodes.rationale: Immovable principle: MicroPython (or console/UDP) is a COMMAND SOURCE, never a control component. No control math — Mahony, PID, mixer, state machine, safety — lives in .py or fc_module.c; all of it is in components/flight_core as plain C that includes nothing from MicroPython or main/. This keeps the realtime loop's timing and correctness independent of the application tier's liveness.

nodes.label: Two-Channel Tier Boundary (command_t down, telemetry_snapshot_t up)
nodes.rationale: The whole boundary is exactly two functions: flight_core_push_command() pushes command_t into a FreeRTOS queue of depth 8 (COMMAND_QUEUE_DEPTH=8) and returns false when full so fc_module.c can raise RuntimeError instead of silently swallowing a command; flight_core_read_telemetry() memcpys telemetry_snapshot_t under a light mutex held only during the copy, not around any logic. No shared pointers, no shared state.

nodes.label: Plain C (not C++) for the lower tier
nodes.rationale: User decision: concern that C++ overhead (RTTI, hidden exceptions, vtables, libstdc++ runtime heap) stacked on top of a MicroPython VM would exhaust RAM/flash on the same chip. All of components/flight_core is plain C — structs and functions, no classes, exceptions or STL.

nodes.label: Single-Writer Principle (only stabilize_task writes control state)
nodes.rationale: Only stabilize_task (hard-pinned to core 1 via xTaskCreatePinnedToCore) writes control state and telemetry — one writer means no race and no heavy locking is needed anywhere in the loop.

nodes.label: Core Affinity Policy (core 1 = flight loop only)
nodes.rationale: Core 1 holds exactly two tasks, both flight loop. Every application/network task pins hard to core 0 because a bare xTaskCreate() on a dual-core build is equivalent to tskNO_AFFINITY and the scheduler may place it on core 1. System tasks count too: lwIP was forced to CONFIG_LWIP_TCPIP_TASK_AFFINITY_CPU0=y since IDF defaults it to NO_AFFINITY. Low priority alone is not enough — it prevents preemption but not cache pollution and dt jitter in core 1's idle slots. CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_AFFINITY_CPU0 pins only the main task and does NOT propagate to tasks it creates, which is why each task must be pinned individually.

nodes.label: KILL — the only hardware touch from core 0
nodes.rationale: flight_core_kill_now() -> motor_driver_all_off() is the single exception that touches hardware from core 0. Because it writes PWM concurrently with core 1, motor_driver.c wraps 'read armed gate + write 4 channels' in a portMUX_TYPE critical section (flow.md 3.7.3).

nodes.label: tuning.h — single tuning file
nodes.rationale: One file collects every tuning constant (angle/rate PID roll-pitch-yaw, alt_hold, takeoff, landing, commander safety), mirroring UAV-Mini's tuning.hpp. Current gains are copied verbatim from UAV-Mini, whose board, motors, props, battery and mass all differ — they MUST be retuned on real S3 hardware, especially ALT_HOLD_HOVER_NOMINAL and TAKEOFF_PRIME_DUTY.

nodes.label: FlightStateMachine (DISARMED/ARMED/TAKING_OFF/HOLDING/FLYING/LANDING/EMERGENCY)
nodes.rationale: EMERGENCY is a TRANSIENT state, resolved inside the same tick it appears (step 7 of stabilize_task) into LANDING (still controllable, airborne) or DISARMED + kill latch (lost control, or still on the ground so there is nothing to 'land').

nodes.label: Commander (safety arbiter)
nodes.rationale: Runs every tick in every armed state. Fault severity is chosen by what keeps the drone alive: heartbeat loss, low battery and estimator loss are SOFT -> LANDING because a hung Python script is routine and must not cut motors mid-air; IMU invalid, |tilt|>60deg and motor saturation >1.5s are HARD -> EMERGENCY. commander_clamp_altitude() is the single geofence chokepoint every write to alt_target_m must pass through.

nodes.label: Heartbeat Watchdog (external-evidence-only)
nodes.rationale: Default 1000ms. The evidence feeding this watchdog must come from OUTSIDE the chip (UDP packet, 'p' from the GUI, fc.heartbeat(), console `heartbeat`) — firmware never generates its own heartbeat, because a self-generated one would prove nothing about the control link still being alive.

nodes.label: Attitude I-term dual gate (FSM gate AND throttle gate)
nodes.rationale: I accumulates only when BOTH independent gates open. Gate 1 keys on liftoff_flag rather than 'PRIME finished', because between leaving TKO_PRIME and actually lifting the controller has already raised throttle while the drone is still pressed against the ground — the prime window for GROUND WINDUP, where I integrates an error that ground reaction (not the motors) is holding, then unloads the instant the drone leaves the ground and flips it. Gate 2 (ATT_I_ENABLE_THROTTLE_DUTY, compared on real duty sent to motors) exists because at low throttle the motors lack authority to generate the correcting moment, so accumulation only breeds windup. ALTITUDE Ki has a wholly separate gate that LIMITS |I| rather than freezing it before liftoff, since the Vz cascade still needs authority to push throttle up to FIND the lift point — hover is only an estimate.

nodes.label: ATT_MIN_THROTTLE_DUTY vs ATT_I_ENABLE_THROTTLE_DUTY
nodes.rationale: Both default to 200 but play different roles: below ATT_MIN_THROTTLE_DUTY the PID does not run at all and the integrator is reset clean; ATT_I_ENABLE_THROTTLE_DUTY only FREEZES I (P/D keep stabilizing, so dropping and re-raising throttle does not lose learned trim). They are kept as two constants so the Ki threshold can be raised during tuning (e.g. 200 -> 400) without touching the PID-run threshold.

nodes.label: I2C Architecture — one shared bus, new i2c_master API
nodes.rationale: flight_core.c::init_i2c_bus() is the ONLY caller of i2c_new_master_bus(); every driver only calls i2c_master_bus_add_device() for its own handle. No driver may call i2c_del_master_bus() or recreate the bus on a read error — errors propagate up as esp_err_t instead of a self-invented loop-reset. This all exists to stop one faulty sensor from hanging the whole bus, a failure actually observed before the refactor. Timeouts pass milliseconds directly (the new API takes ms, not pdMS_TO_TICKS).

nodes.label: I2C 100kHz debug-phase speed (later 400kHz)
nodes.rationale: BOARD_I2C_FREQ_HZ plus four per-driver *_I2C_SCL_SPEED_HZ macros are held at 100kHz to confirm MPU6050+QMC5883P+BMP280 are stable on the new bus architecture first; raising to 400000 requires editing BOTH board_config.h and all four driver macros because there is not yet one shared configuration point.

nodes.label: BMP280 init separated from ground-zero calibration
nodes.rationale: baro_driver_init() only brings the chip to an operable state (probe CHIP_ID, wait for NVM copy via STATUS.im_update, validate the calibration table, write CONFIG/CTRL_MEAS with read-back verify) and deliberately no longer captures the 0m reference. baro_driver_calibrate_ground() is a separate step (300ms settle + average of 32 valid samples) and baro_driver_read() returns ok=false until it succeeds, so a missing ground reference fails loudly instead of producing plausible-but-wrong altitude.

nodes.label: Altitude Estimator (accel-primary, ToF/baro anchor)
nodes.rationale: Vz comes from integrating world-frame gravity-removed acceleration; VL53L0X and BMP280 are ONLY anchors applied through small alpha/beta corrections. Their derivative is never taken as Vz and the estimate is never snapped to a measurement, because both sensors are far too noisy per-sample. ToF is ~cm accurate versus baro's +-0.3-1m but is range-limited (~1.8m) and measures the surface directly beneath (flying over a table changes the surface), so baro is still required for high or long flights. Losing BOTH sources longer than ALT_EST_NO_CORRECTION_DEGRADED_MS makes Commander force LANDING. Three states form a hand-rolled alpha-beta-gamma filter: alt_m, vz_ms, and accel_bias_ms2 learned very slowly (0.03Hz) only while DISARMED and truly stationary, with ZUPT forcing vz_ms to 0.

nodes.label: Motor vibration filtering — hardware DLPF first, software LPF second
nodes.rationale: Because Vz relies mainly on accel integration and ToF/baro only pull back slowly, the primary defense is the MPU6050 hardware DLPF (IMU_ACCEL_DLPF_CFG=3 -> 44Hz, written straight to CONFIG register 0x1A) filtering before the numbers reach the MCU; the software LPF in alt_estimator.c (10Hz) plus a deadband is only the second layer. Test G says: if Az still picks up motor-frequency vibration, lower IMU_ACCEL_DLPF_CFG before suspecting the software LPF.

nodes.label: seq-based sample consumption (replaces tick divisors)
nodes.rationale: 'Do not reuse one sample many times' is enforced through each sensor's seq counter: alt_estimator_update() receives raw seq + timestamp for baro/ToF and decides what it has already consumed. BARO_READ_TICK_DIVISOR was removed because tick counting is only correct when the read cadence lines up exactly with a multiple of the control cadence, whereas seq stays correct even when the hub is late or drops a sample. Running a correction 5x more often than intended pulls Z toward baro 5x as hard and looks from outside exactly like 'Z refuses to climb'.

nodes.label: liftoff_flag — simple Z threshold, gates nothing
nodes.rationale: est_z > ground_alt_m + TAKEOFF_LIFTOFF_DELTA_M (0.05m). It changes no controller, no phase, and no estimator state — it only feeds telemetry, widens the |I| ceiling, and tells EMERGENCY whether the drone is airborne. The previous 4-evidence scorer (THR/ACC/VZ/Z, >=3/4) existed because the flag then gated both the estimator and altitude Ki, where a false report ruined the flight; now that it gates nothing, one Z threshold is sufficient and far easier to reason about. Telemetry LSC (liftoff score) is therefore always 0, kept only so old GUI regexes do not break. Baro is never the liftoff detector — near the ground is exactly where baro is weakest (propwash + ground effect).

nodes.label: Calibration persistence in NVS (gyro / accel / mag)
nodes.rationale: Three independent fields in NVS namespace fc_calib, each with its own CRC32 plus one shared CALIB_NVS_FORMAT_VERSION, so a corrupt field invalidates only itself and a future struct-layout change makes new firmware treat old NVS as UNCALIBRATED instead of reading garbage. Accel/mag math is orientation-agnostic (per-axis min/max across many placements, never hard-assigning 'this face = this axis'), so it is safe to run BEFORE the IMU/mag axis remap is confirmed. No calibration runs automatically: boot only loads what NVS already holds, so gyro-bias thermal drift between flights must be handled by explicitly running calib_gyro before arm.

nodes.label: BREAKING CHANGE — ARM refused without valid accel calibration
nodes.rationale: CMD_ARM (console `arm`, fc.arm(), @ARM over UDP — all funnelling through apply_command() in flight_core.c) is now REFUSED unless valid accel calibration exists in NVS (plus mag when SENSOR_MAG_ENABLED=1). On a first flash with empty NVS the drone cannot arm until calibrated once.

nodes.label: 6-face accel calibration verify (residual gate)
nodes.rationale: After 6-face collection the bias/scale correction is re-applied to the same six faces and residual = ||a_corrected| - 1.0g| is checked; exceeding CALIB_ACCEL_MAX_RESIDUAL_G (0.15g) DISCARDS everything rather than saving a fit that only looks converged.

nodes.label: Deliberately not implemented (self-test, ellipsoid soft-iron, thermal comp, CompassMot)
nodes.rationale: Four omissions are choices, not oversights. MPU6050 self-test needs exact datasheet register bit layout that was not confidently recalled — a mis-transcribed version produces fake PASS/FAIL, which is more dangerous than nothing. Full 3x3 ellipsoid soft-iron fit belongs OFFLINE on a PC (least-squares) with the matrix uploaded, not on the ESP32; diagonal per-axis is enough for Mahony normalization. Thermal compensation only logs imu_temp_c until a real dataset exists to fit a polynomial. CompassMot is not invented without a current sensor; it is checked manually via existing mag-raw + throttle telemetry.

nodes.label: Battery throttle compensation — removed
nodes.rationale: throttle_cmd *= clamp(4.2/battery_v, 1.0, 1.25) was deleted outright because it is control-theoretically wrong: measured VBAT sags with INSTANTANEOUS LOAD, not just remaining charge, so multiplying throttle by it creates a parasitic positive feedback loop outside every tuned PID (throttle up -> current up -> measured VBAT down -> comp up -> throttle up). It also broke alt_hold since the real duty at the motors stopped matching what the PID asked for, invalidating bench-tuned gains. Bench logs measured BATV swinging 3.51-3.82V at near-constant load, i.e. comp jumping 1.10-1.20 — voltage noise amplified straight into throttle. Battery voltage is still used for the failsafe floor and prearm_check, which are THRESHOLD comparisons, not multiplications into the control path. BCOMP telemetry is pinned at 1.000 to keep the STATUS line format stable.

nodes.label: 11-bit motor PWM at 24kHz
nodes.rationale: Raised from 10-bit (0-1023, MOTOR_SAFE_MAX_DUTY=1000) to 11-bit (0-2047, max 2000) while keeping 24kHz, because the 80MHz APB clock divides adequately for 2^11 but not for 2^12. Every duty-unit constant in tuning.h was doubled to match; deg/dps/m/(m/s)-unit constants were untouched since they do not live on the duty scale.

nodes.label: Console and flashing over USB D+/D- (USB-Serial-JTAG)
nodes.rationale: miniUav has no USB-UART bridge chip, so flashing, logs and the REPL all use the ESP32-S3's built-in USB-Serial-JTAG controller on IO19/IO20. Without a bridge chip to toggle DTR/RTS, download mode must be entered MANUALLY (hold BOOT, press/release RESET, release BOOT). sdkconfig must set CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_USB_SERIAL_JTAG=y — ESP-IDF's default of UART0 would be completely silent because UART0 is not wired on this board.

nodes.label: main/board_config.h — real pins from the miniUav schematic
nodes.rationale: Answers 'which pin' — I2C SDA=IO44/SCL=IO43, MPU_INT=IO36, ToF XSHUT IO17/IO18, motors IO4/IO8/IO39/IO1, battery ADC IO6 (divider 3.2), BMP280 at 0x77 and QMC5883P at 0x2C (both confirmed by bus scan; QMC5883P is a completely different part from the originally assumed QMC5883L, with a different register map and chip ID).

nodes.label: main/app_config.h — sensor enable flags and motor confirmation
nodes.rationale: The second file (with board_config.h) that fc_bridge.c and src/main.c include to build flight_core_board_config_t. board_config.h answers 'which pin'; app_config.h answers 'which one is IN USE'. Setting a SENSOR_*_ENABLED flag to 0 makes flight_core_start() skip that driver's init entirely — no I2C probing, no noisy warnings — and takes effect on rebuild without editing flight_core.c.

nodes.label: Unconfirmed physical motor positions CH1..CH4 (flight blocker)
nodes.rationale: board_config.h/fc_bridge.c currently map CH1->M1..CH4->M4 following schematic NET ORDER only; nobody has verified which frame corner CH1 is or its CW/CCW rotation. attitude_control.h assumes Quad-X M1=front-left, M2=front-right, M3=back-right, M4=back-left. A wrong mapping here flips the drone the instant it arms and no amount of tuning can rescue it, so the confirmation procedure is empirical, never inferred: remove all props, run `test_motor <n> <duty>` (DISARMED-only, enforced by flight_core.c::apply_command()), record which arm spins, then fix motor_gpio[0..3] ordering. MOTOR_POSITIONS_CONFIRMED does not block build or arm — it only prints a boot warning — so the checklist must be completed by discipline, not by the code.

nodes.label: Control loop clocked by MPU6050 data-ready interrupt (IO36)
nodes.rationale: The sample is read as soon as it is produced and reaches the control loop BEFORE the hub touches any slower sensor, so latency is small and — more importantly — STABLE: no 0-4ms jitter from phase drift between the FreeRTOS clock and the sensor's internal clock. For a control loop, latency jitter is noise injected straight into the D-term. Requires IMU_SAMPLE_RATE_HZ == CONTROL_TASK_HZ, guarded by _Static_assert, with SMPLRT_DIV derived rather than hand-set.

nodes.label: Interrupt-loss fallback to the FreeRTOS clock
nodes.rationale: The notify wait always carries a timeout (2 periods); missing IMU_INT_MISS_STREAK_MAX consecutive edges (~100ms) falls back to the FreeRTOS clock and logs an error. The control loop must NEVER block indefinitely on an interrupt: if the INT wire breaks mid-flight, a stalled task means motors hold their last duty AND Commander/failsafe stop running too. Running on the fallback clock does not mean integrating stale samples — on a tick with no new IMU sample (seq unchanged or sample expired) Mahony, alt_estimator and the PID I-term are all skipped, while safety/deadline/failsafe/Commander/mixer still run.

nodes.label: GPIO33-37 PSRAM octal bus conflict with MPU_INT
nodes.rationale: IO36 is only usable for the IMU interrupt because PSRAM is disabled (CONFIG_SPIRAM is not set). Enabling PSRAM claims that pin and silently breaks the IMU interrupt — the fix is to relocate INT, not to debug the MPU6050.

nodes.label: mag_test — QMC5883P hardware diagnostic (not calibration)
nodes.rationale: If calib_mag collects 0 samples, more rotating is pointless — the chip is not producing samples, which is a hardware question, not a technique question. mag_test re-runs the whole init sequence logging every step and reads at 50Hz against a 100Hz ODR so ok% is the verdict. Running it with and without writing REG 0x29=0x06 settles empirically whether this part needs that write: the QST datasheet says yes, but this hardware has been observed to return CTRL2 readback 0x00 after writing 0x29. Main firmware currently does NOT write 0x29, and changing that decision must rest on real mag_test logs rather than the datasheet alone.

nodes.label: bench_start / +/- / bench_stop — manual throttle ramp for PID tuning
nodes.rationale: For tuning PID without flying, with the drone clamped to a rig — explicitly NOT a flight mode. Attitude PID engages at the very same ATT_MIN_THROTTLE_DUTY threshold as every other state, with no bench-specific logic path, so what is tuned here is what flies. FSM_BENCH_RAMP is wrapped by the full common safety stack (tilt/attitude-stale kill latch, Commander heartbeat/battery/hard-tilt). bench_stop does not latch, so it can be re-entered.

nodes.label: Firmware background heartbeat task (300ms)
nodes.rationale: A dedicated task emits a heartbeat every 300ms so the Commander watchdog does not soft-fault merely because the operator is reading logs between console commands. Known limitation: since that task is independent of the console task, a hung console is NOT caught by this watchdog — but the other safety layers (immediate motor cut on tilt/attitude-stale, battery floor, IMU-invalid) do not depend on heartbeat and remain independent.

nodes.label: Yaw drift without magnetometer (known limitation #1)
nodes.rationale: flight_core.c only treats mag as valid when mag_driver_read() returns ok=true, so a missing or faulty chip degrades automatically to 'no mag' — safe by design. But with ATT_GAIN_ANGLE_YAW_KP=0 by default (heading-hold off, pure rate yaw), gyro Z bias is never corrected, so the drone slowly rotates even at yaw_rate=0. set_yaw(deg) is likewise open-loop in time rather than absolute heading, for the same missing-mag reason.

nodes.label: IMU/mag axis remap unconfirmed (known limitation #6)
nodes.rationale: imu_driver.c/mag_driver.c map sensor x/y/z straight to body axes because the real mounting orientation on the frame is unknown. Unlike a wrong motor mapping this will not flip the drone immediately, but Mahony converges with wrong roll/pitch/yaw sign — check by tilting the board on a desk and comparing readings.

nodes.label: ToF ST ULD tuning table — present (README correction #5)
nodes.rationale: The earlier claim that the tuning table was missing was itself wrong. tof_driver.c has the complete 80-pair VL53L0X_TUNING[] table matching the ST ULD/Pololu reference plus the full init chain (DataInit with 2V8 + stop_variable, StaticInit with get_spad_info() and ref SPAD map, new-sample interrupt config, 33ms timing budget, VHV + phase ref calibration, continuous back-to-back), and TOF_CONFIG_TODO no longer exists in source. Bench-testing is still mandatory, but for a different reason: offset/crosstalk have not been calibrated for the SPECIFIC cover glass on this frame.
